title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
Agents build the transition pipeline with the recommended coding of every open hard case (Section 3), marked DRAFT. Nothing built from a DRAFT coding is ACTIVE until the user says so.
At gate G0, which is asked at the start of the run and before anything is built, the user confirms or flips each open case (decision D10). The wave-1 integrator records the answers in the Status and User note lines of this sheet and in reports/GATE-G0.md. A flip is applied once, by package WP99, to the contract seeds (contract/label_triage.csv, codes.csv, legacy_overrides.csv), and contract/check_contract.R recomputes the expected counts. Every later package then builds the flipped coding from the start.
Related documents: plan, contract, package cards, standard, input findings.

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.1 H1 — Non-food consumption share
Case. Whether label #72, “Non-food consumption share”, is stored as its own series or derived from COICOP 1.
Evidence. Food share + non-food share sums to 0.98–1.02 across cells; non-food minus the sum of COICOP 2–13 sits in −0.02 to +0.03. This follows the standard’s existing precedent of not storing a separate “housing burden” indicator (data-standard.qmd line 73).
Recommended (built default). DERIVED, not stored as its own series: value = 1 − CONS_SH/COICOP_CP01.
Alternative. An aggregate qualifier COICOP_CP02T13 — needs an aggregate-category flag the standard does not have, and the closure check currently excludes aggregates.
Built by. WP08 (SERIES_PLAN.csv — no series row for label #72), WP09 (LEGACY_LABELS.csv assert_rule: ONE_MINUS:<label#>).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

section: 3.2 H2 — Own-production vs. market food share
text:
3.2 H2 — Own-production vs. market food share
Case. Whether label #77 “Own-production food share” and label #69 “Market food share” are a new qualifier on CONS_SH + COICOP 1, or two separate indicators.
Evidence. Own-production share + market share is less than the food share by 0.01–0.03 in SEN and 0.03–0.08 in GNB — the gap is gifts/in-kind acquisition, and there is no closure check across the three.
Recommended (built default). A new qualifier variable ACQ (acquisition mode) on CONS_SH + COICOP_CP01, categories ACQ_PURCH, ACQ_OWNPROD (DRAFT categories ACQ_GIFT, ACQ_INKIND registered but not populated).
Alternative. Two separate indicators, CONS_FOOD_OWN_SH and CONS_FOOD_MKT_SH.
Built by. WP06 (CL_QUAL_VAR.csv, CL_QUALIFIER.csv — the ACQ variable and its categories), WP08 (SERIES_PLAN.csv), WP09 (legacy maps).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.3 H3 — Wage vs. non-wage employment
Case. Whether label #95 “Wage-employed” and label #73 “Non-wage employed” need a new breakdown variable or a derived indicator.
Evidence. Wage share + non-wage share sums to exactly 1.00 in every cell of both countries.
Recommended (built default). POP_SH with a new breakdown variable EMP_TYPE (categories EMP_TYPE_WAGE, EMP_TYPE_NONWAGE, ICSE-based).
Alternative. A single proportion indicator JOB_WAGE, with non-wage DERIVED as 1 − JOB_WAGE.
Built by. WP06 (CL_BRK_VAR.csv, CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN.csv — EMP_TYPE), WP08 (SERIES_PLAN.csv), WP09 (legacy maps).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.4 H4 — “Employed”
Case. Whether label #26 “Employed (activ12m, 15–64)” also needs a derived “not employed” row.
Evidence. No cross-check issue found; the existing breakdown variable EMP_STATUS already has both categories (EMP_STATUS_EMPLOYED, EMP_STATUS_NOT_EMPLOYED — see the standard’s initial breakdown variables table, sec-initial-breakdowns), but only the employed category is populated by the legacy label.
Recommended (built default). Map to POP_SH with breakdown EMP_STATUS_EMPLOYED only; EMP_STATUS_NOT_EMPLOYED is never derived from it, since no legacy label provides an independent value to check against.
Alternative. None proposed in the report.
Built by. WP09 (LEGACY_LABELS.csv mapping only; no new codelist rows).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.5 H5 — “HH workers” in trade/transport
Case. Whether labels #89 “Share of HH workers in trade/commerce” and #90 “…in transport” are children of EMP_SECTOR_SER or a new breakdown variable, and what “HH workers” means as a universe.
Evidence. Trade + transport is always ≤ services (gap 0.00–0.36 across cells), consistent with being subsets of it. The universe “HH workers” is not otherwise defined in the legacy labels.
Recommended (built default). POP_SH with a new breakdown variable EMP_ISIC (ISIC sections; register the full A–U set, publish sections G and H). Universe left TBD.
Alternative. Nest trade and transport as children of EMP_SECTOR_SER, or register them as separate JOB_* proportion indicators.
Built by. WP06 (CL_BRK_VAR.csv, CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN.csv — EMP_ISIC), WP08 (SERIES_PLAN.csv), WP09 (legacy maps).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.6 H6 — “HH workers” informally employed
Case. Whether label #91 “Share of HH workers informally employed” is a new breakdown of the employed, or of wage employees only.
Evidence. Correlates with the non-wage share at r = 0.86–1.00, and sits 0.01–0.04 below it. This contradicts how the dashboard currently labels the equivalent figure, “Informal wage employment (% of wage)” (index.qmd:93), which implies a wage-employee universe.
Recommended (built default). POP_SH with a new breakdown variable EMP_FORMAL (categories EMP_FORMAL_Y, publish EMP_FORMAL_N), universe = employed persons, marked DRAFT.
Alternative. Universe = wage employees only, matching how the dashboard currently reads the figure.
Built by. WP06 (CL_BRK_VAR.csv, CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN.csv — EMP_FORMAL), WP08 (SERIES_PLAN.csv), WP09 (legacy maps).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.7 H7 — Three electricity indicators
Case. Whether labels #1 “Access to electricity (grid, SDG 7.1.1)”, #17 “Connected to electricity grid (SDG7.1.1)” and #93 “Uses grid electricity” are three distinct indicators or duplicates of one concept.
Evidence. The three differ by country: GNB national totals are 0.23 / 0.27 / 0.26 (a narrow spread), but SEN’s are 0.68 / 0.98 / 0.66 (a 32-point spread) — the definitions clearly differ but are undocumented. On SEN, EN_GRID_CONN (#17) is 0.96–1.00 in every cell, including Q1 and Rural, which cannot be true grid connection of essentially all households. SDG 7.1.1 is normally population-based, so the weight needs confirming.
Recommended (built default). Three DRAFT codes (EN_ELEC_ACCESS, EN_GRID_CONN, EN_GRID_USE) cross-linked with related/related_note; a COMMENT override on the SEN EN_GRID_CONN rows noting the implausible near-universal value.
Alternative. Skip EN_GRID_CONN in both countries until its definition is documented.
Built by. WP07 (CL_INDICATOR.csv — the three codes and their related fields), WP09 (LEGACY_OVERRIDES.csv COMMENT on SEN EN_GRID_CONN).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.8 H8 — Average outage duration (code)
Case. Whether label #3 “Average outage duration (code)” — a mean of an ordinal code, not a time unit — can be mapped at all.
Evidence. The value is explicitly a mean of a code (Annex 1 of the standard), not a duration; the code scale itself is not documented anywhere in the legacy files.
Recommended (built default). Map as DRAFT, unit_measure INDEX, checked with RANGE_NONNEG only; flagged for later deprecation in favour of shares by duration class once the code scale is documented.
Alternative. Skip #3 until the code scale is documented.
Built by. WP07 (CL_INDICATOR.csv — EN_OUTAGE_DUR_CODE, unit_measure INDEX), WP09 (legacy map).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.9 H9 — Cooker “proxy”
Case. Whether label #86 “Proxy: owns gas/electric cooker (cuisin)” is mapped as a proxy for label #85 “Primary cooking fuel clean (gas/electricity)”, and whether the “proxy” wording belongs in the indicator name.
Evidence. SEN clean-cooking share is 0.73 nationally against a cooker-ownership share of only 0.04, and clean cooking is higher in Rural (0.76) than Capital (0.60) and higher for Q1 (0.79) than Q4 (0.57) — the reverse of what “clean cooking” should show, and implausible on its face.
Recommended (built default). EN_ASSET_COOKER, “proxy” dropped from the name, related = EN_COOK_CLEAN; both flagged for human review given the implausible pattern.
Alternative. Skip label #86 entirely.
Built by. WP07 (CL_INDICATOR.csv — name and related field), WP09 (legacy map, LEGACY_OVERRIDES.csv COMMENT).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.10 H10 — Owner vs. owns enterprise
Case. Whether label #59 “HH has non-agric enterprise owner” and label #60 “HH owns a non-agric enterprise” are the same fact from two sources, or two different indicators.
Evidence. Label #60 equals 1 − (label #53, “HH has 0 HE”) exactly in every cell of both countries. Label #59 differs from #60 by −0.28 to +0.39, so it comes from a different source variable, not a rounding difference.
Recommended (built default). #60 is DERIVED (not stored); #59 is mapped as a new DRAFT indicator HE_HH_OWNER.
Alternative. Code #60 as POP_HH_SH with a new aggregate breakdown category HE_COUNT_1P (parent of HE_COUNT_1…HE_COUNT_4P).
Built by. WP07 (CL_INDICATOR.csv — HE_HH_OWNER), WP09 (LEGACY_LABELS.csv assert_rule: ONE_MINUS:<label#> for #60).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.11 H11 — HE owner female / married
Case. Whether labels #67 “Main HE owner is female” and #68 “Main HE owner is married” are breakdown categories of POP_HE_SH or their own proportion indicators.
Evidence. No cross-check contradiction found; the choice is structural — the standard has no rule yet for “share as a breakdown vs. share as a proportion indicator” (see gap (o)/(t) discussion and Section 5 item 7 area).
Recommended (built default). POP_HE_SH with two new breakdown variables, HEO_SEX (categories HEO_SEX_F, publish HEO_SEX_M) and HEO_MSTAT (categories HEO_MSTAT_MARRIED, HEO_MSTAT_NOT_MARRIED), so either can also break down other HE indicators.
Alternative. Two proportion indicators, HE_OWNER_FEMALE and HE_OWNER_MARRIED.
Built by. WP06 (CL_BRK_VAR.csv, CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN.csv — HEO_SEX, HEO_MSTAT), WP08 (SERIES_PLAN.csv), WP09 (legacy maps).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.12 H12 — HE external employees
Case. Whether label #38 “HE has external (non-HH) employees” can be mapped as-is.
Evidence. The share is 0.96 (SEN) / 1.00 (GNB) — impossible for “all HEs have external employees” when mean non-HH employees (label #71) is only 0.54/0.48. Label #74 “Number of employees in HE” does not equal #52 + #71 (residual −0.53 to +1.96 in SEN, −0.76 to +0.09 in GNB), so there is no additive check to fall back on.
Recommended (built default). Map DRAFT, universe TBD, with a COMMENT override noting the implausible near-universal value.
Alternative. Skip label #38.
Built by. WP07 (CL_INDICATOR.csv — universe_filter), WP09 (LEGACY_OVERRIDES.csv COMMENT).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.13 H13 — ≥1 HH member covered
Case. Whether label #97 “≥1 HH member has health coverage (proxy social protection)” is a household-level indicator or a breakdown of label #62 “Has health insurance/coverage (couvmal)”.
Evidence. Always ≥ label #62 by 0.00–0.08, consistent with “at least one member” being a looser condition than the individual-level question.
Recommended (built default). A new household-level indicator SP_HEALTH_COV_HH; “proxy social protection” kept only in notes, not the name.
Alternative. POP_HH_SH with a new breakdown variable.
Built by. WP07 (CL_INDICATOR.csv — SP_HEALTH_COV_HH), WP09 (legacy map).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

3.14 H14 — Internet access
Case. Whether label #58 “HH has internet access” is worth mapping at all.
Evidence. 0.00 or empty in every cell of both countries — implausible for SEN in particular, and carries no information.
Recommended (built default). SKIP.
Alternative. Map it with a COMMENT override instead of skipping.
Built by. WP09 (LEGACY_LABELS.csv, action SKIP).

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.15 H15 — Share indicators’ unit
Case. Whether population shares need one indicator (POP_SH) or several, split by the statistical unit of the breakdown behind them.
Evidence. A single POP_SH cannot keep one stat_unit: HE_COUNT breakdowns describe households (standard line 77) while POP_SH’s declared stat_unit is IND (standard line 386).
Decision. DECIDED by D4 (Table 1): three codes, POP_SH (IND), POP_HH_SH (HH), POP_HE_SH (HE), each with its matching weight.
Alternative (not taken). One POP_SH with stat_unit inferred from the breakdown’s describes field.
Built by. WP07 (CL_INDICATOR.csv — the three codes).
Status. DECIDED — D4.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.16 H16 — Departement sheet
Case. Whether to load any of the Departement sheet’s 82 labels.
Evidence. Its poverty totals disagree with ADM 1 (4.13M/7.88M vs 3.13M/6.52M poor), and several values that should match a shared indicator are impossible (HE has any credit access = 1.00 in every region; HH has 4+ HE = 0.80–1.00, though 0/1/2/3 already sum to about 1).
Decision. DECIDED by D3 (Table 1): skip all 82 labels.
Alternative (not taken). Keep the sheet’s two poverty rows as POV_HC with PPP_2017.
Built by. WP02 (standard text — removes the PPP_2017 exception and example row, closes open decision 9), WP09 (LEGACY_LABELS.csv, action SKIP).
Status. DECIDED — D3.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.17 H17 — Household-head age cutoff
Case. Where the boundary between Youth_HH and Older_HH falls, since the legacy files never document it.
Evidence. The dashboard currently labels Older_HH as “29+” (index.qmd:64), which contradicts the standard’s placeholder HHH_AGE_LT35/HHH_AGE_GE35 (standard lines 296, 905) and suggests a cutoff of 29 or 30, not 35.
Recommended (built default). DRAFT codes that stay renamable without becoming a new code (per the “never changes meaning” rule, standard line 373 — a DRAFT code can still be corrected); confirm the true cutoff with the producer before the codes go ACTIVE.
Alternative. Keep HHH_AGE_LT35/HHH_AGE_GE35 as written in the standard.
Built by. WP06 (CL_BRK_VAR.csv, CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN.csv — the HHH_AGE categories).
Status. DEFAULT.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.18 H18 — GNB Capital column
Case. Whether to keep the GNB National estimateCapital column, given it does not hold Bissau’s values.
Evidence. estimateCapital is byte-identical to ZAE estimateZonas_Costeiras_do_Sul on all 97 indicators, and matches SAB (Bissau) on only 9 of 97 rows — all rows that are constant everywhere anyway. Keeping it with AGG_SUM would fail: residence shares would sum to 1.24M poor at $4.20 against a national 1.09M.
Decision. DECIDED by D5 (Table 1): withheld — the whole column is absent as rows, registered in LEGACY_OVERRIDES.csv.
Alternative (not taken). Keep it with a COMMENT override, accepting that AGG_SUM would fail on it.
Built by. WP09 (LEGACY_OVERRIDES.csv, action WITHHOLD).
Status. DECIDED — D5.
User note. —

title: Appendix B.3. AFW 360 transition: decisions
text:
3.19 H19 — GNB cultivated area
Case. Whether to keep the 7 GNB Cultivated area (ha) cells above 100 ha outside the Capital column.
Evidence. Values reach the millions of “ha” (National Total 9.1M, Rural 10.8M, Male_HH 10.4M, Older_HH 10.5M, Q4 57.9M; ADM 1 Quinara 148.4M; ZAE Zonas_Costeiras_do_Sul 53.0M), against 1–15 ha for the rest of the indicator — almost certainly outlier records from a unit error in the microdata, each inflating the mean it enters.
Decision. DECIDED by D5 (Table 1): withhold these 7 cells (plus Capital’s own cell, already withheld under H18).
Alternative (not taken). Withhold the whole AGR_CULT_AREA indicator for GNB (26 rows), rather than just the affected cells.
Built by. WP09 (LEGACY_OVERRIDES.csv, action WITHHOLD, 7 rows).
Status. DECIDED — D5.
User note. —

This plan converts the dashboard’s current inputs (two Excel workbooks, 22 shapefile layers, a handful of text files and one image) into the files defined by the data standard:
Every file is produced by R code under pipeline/, so the conversion can be read, rerun and checked. The dashboard keeps working throughout, and it switches to the new files only after this plan is complete.

2.2 What shapes the transition
The full findings are in input-tables-findings.qmd.

Each sheet is a set of one-way breakdowns of the national population. Breakdowns are never crossed.

text:
5.1 Principles

Small context.

An agent reads COMMON.md, its card, and a few filtered rows: about 10,000 to 25,000 tokens.
Its whole session stays under 100,000 tokens, and 150,000 is the hard limit.
An agent that runs long stops, and reports PARTIAL. A fresh agent then continues.

Contract first. The packages of a wave build against the contract seeds, not against each other’s output. contract/check_contract.R proves that the seeds agree with each other and with the workbooks.
Code, not typing.

Metadata files are generated by scripts from the seeds.
Agents write text (names, definitions) only where there is no source for it.
Every generator can rebuild into a temporary directory, so any file can be checked by regenerating it.

Real inputs for the validator. The validator is written in wave 3 against the real, merged metadata, never against invented fixtures.
Ownership. Every output path has exactly one owner in contract/output_ownership.csv. An agent that needs another path stops and reports.
Independent verification. The verifier writes its own acceptance script from the card. The scripts are kept, and they are rerun after every merge.
State in git. Branch names and commit subjects (WP05: verify v1 - VERDICT: PASS) record the state of the run. A new orchestrator session resumes from them.
Nothing is pushed, and nothing reaches dev/eb before the user says so at G2.

After every merge, the integrator reruns every acceptance script written so far, plus the unit tests. A failure is reported against the package that owns the broken file, and that package gets a patch agent. The integrator never fixes anything. It ends with one of three statuses: INTEGRATED; FINDINGS, when every failure has an owning package, so patch agents are sent without asking the user; or BLOCKED, when a branch cannot be merged or a failure has no owner, which goes to the user. A failed WP17 audit is handled like integrator findings: patches, a follow-up wave-3 integration, then the audit again as v2. Validator findings on the real data at wave 3 go first to the package that owns the check (FINDINGS mode): that agent decides, from its card’s rules, whether the check or the data is wrong.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
This document defines how data for the West Africa Micro Data 360 platform (AFW 360) are structured, coded and documented, how producers create data files, and how the database is extended to new countries, indicators and breakdowns. It follows the SDMX information model (the ISO standard statistical agencies use to exchange data) and borrows the World Bank Data360 dimension layout, stored as plain CSV files in git.
Background on the current inputs is in input-tables-findings.qmd. Nothing here changes the current INPUT Tables/ files. A Python converter will produce the new files from them, and the dashboard will switch over later.
How to read this document. Section 1 is the whole idea on one page: the model, where every file lives, and how the database grows. Read it first. Sections 2 to 11 are reference material; come back to them when you need the exact rule. Section 12 records the design decisions already taken and those still open. Table 1 suggests where to start.

1.1 One row is one number
Each row of a data file carries one value and the full set of codes that say what that value is: which country, which year, which population, which measure. Those codes fall into two families (Table 2), and telling them apart is the whole model.

The quickest test is the population. If the people behind the categories add up to the whole, as regions or quintiles do, the variable is a breakdown. If every category covers the same whole population again, as the $3.00 and $4.20 poverty lines do, it is a qualifier. N_POP, the population behind each row, makes the test mechanical.
This matters for three reasons. The poverty rate at any line and PPP round is one indicator, POV_HC, not one per line. Every population share is one indicator, POP_SH, not thirty. And a new grouping such as sector of employment is a row in a codelist, not a change to the file format.
This distinction is the foundation of the database. Every rule in the rest of this document follows from it, and everyone who adds data has to apply it consistently.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
1.4 How the database grows
The rule for every extension is metadata first, data last. A number can enter the database only once its codes exist, so every change starts in the codelists and ends with a data file that the validator accepts. If a new number cannot be described with the existing codes, the codes are extended first, in the same pull request as the data.
A new country is added in this order:

Register the country in CL_AREA.
Register its spatial schemes in CL_GEO_SCHEME and their units in CL_GEO.
Check its indicators against the dictionary, CL_INDICATOR. Every country should produce the same set of indicators, matching the dictionary’s codes, definitions and meaning. When a country’s survey cannot match a definition, update the dictionary with a new code linked to the old one through related, rather than stretching an existing code to fit.
Do the same for breakdowns and qualifiers: the country’s categories map to the shared codes in CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN and CL_QUALIFIER.
Describe the survey in SURVEYS.csv, and add the boundary files the maps need.
Produce the data file for each reference year, following TAB_PLAN, together with its manifest.

Section 7.4 gives each step in full.
A new indicator starts in the microdata, not in the aggregation. First standardize the variables it needs in the survey microdata itself, so that each one has the same definition, universe, unit and recall period in every country. Once they are standardized, the indicator is a simple aggregate of them: a mean, a share or a total over each cut. If an indicator needs complicated logic at the aggregation step, its variables are not yet standardized enough.
Every constructed variable also needs its own metadata, recording what the microdata looked like when the indicator was computed from it: the questionnaire module and questions, the recall period, the universe, the units and any recoding. CL_INDICATOR points to these variables through source_questionnaire, source_vars and program. Where the variable-level documentation itself is kept is still an open decision (Section 12.2).
Everything else, such as a breakdown, a qualifier, a poverty line, a spatial scheme, a survey round, a piece of text or a figure, is listed in Table 18 with the files to edit and the version bump it needs. The only structural change is to the columns of the data file, and only the data team makes it (Section 10).

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
2.2 The two sentinels
_T and _Z are reserved codes with fixed meanings. They are never listed in a codelist, and no other code may start with them.

_T, total. The value covers every unit and is not split on this dimension. Valid in GEO, SEX, AGE, URBANISATION and the breakdown slots.
_Z, not applicable. Valid in every unused qualifier slot, and in SEX or AGE when the indicator is not about individuals. A household-level indicator writes SEX=_Z, not SEX=_T, because “total over both sexes” would be a claim about a dimension that does not apply to households.
GEO and URBANISATION are never _Z: every unit lives somewhere.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
2.3 Rules for the breakdown columns

Fill the slots from the left, with no gaps. Unused slots are _T.
Use the canonical order. When a row has several breakdowns, they go in ascending slot_order from CL_BRK_VAR, with ties broken alphabetically by var_code. Each combination then has exactly one spelling.
One category per variable per row.
Respect unit compatibility. A breakdown variable may be used only with indicators whose stat_unit appears in its applies_to_units.
Never duplicate a named dimension. Residence, individual sex, individual age and geography always go in their own columns.
SEX and AGE describe the individual being counted, not the household head. The head’s characteristics are breakdown variables (HHH_SEX, HHH_AGE) and go in the slots.
An age band that defines an indicator’s universe is not a breakdown. “Employed, 15–64” has that band in its universe and writes AGE=_T.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
2.4 Rules for the qualifier columns

Fill from the left, with no gaps. Unused slots are _Z.
Use the canonical order: ascending slot_order from CL_QUAL_VAR, with ties broken alphabetically.
One category per qualifier variable per row.
A row may use only the qualifiers its indicator declares in CL_INDICATOR.qualifiers, plus any qualifier required by a breakdown it uses. POOR_Y requires a poverty line, so a food-share row broken down by poverty status carries POVLINE_* and PPP_* even though CONS_SH does not otherwise use them.
Pairings must be allowed: CL_QUALIFIER.valid_with says which PPP rounds go with which line.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
2.5 Values and attributes

Store OBS_VALUE unrounded, with . as the decimal separator and no thousands separator or % sign. Rounding is a display decision (display_as, decimals).
Use base units. Shares are 0–1, never 0–100. People are counted in persons, not millions. Money is in whole currency units.
Do not suppress. Every estimate is published whatever its sample size. Reliability travels with the value instead: N_OBS and N_POP are required on every row, STD_ERR and the confidence interval on every row whose statistic admits them, and the dashboard shows them (Section 6.3).
N_OBS is the unweighted number of records of the estimation file used: records in the group, in the indicator’s universe, with a non-missing value. When a person-weighted poverty rate is computed on a household file, N_OBS counts households. SURVEYS.analysis_units records which file each stat_unit is estimated from, so a reader always knows what N_OBS counts.
N_POP is the sum of weights over those same records: the population, households or enterprises the value refers to.
Standard errors and confidence intervals must reflect the survey design (weights, strata and PSUs, with linearized variance). Intervals are at 95%.

OBS_STATUS takes one of the four codes in Table 5, which come from the SDMX cross-domain CL_OBS_STATUS. A cell that can never exist is normally declared in the indicator’s excluded_breakdowns (Section 5.2) and left out of the file. M covers such a cell when it has not been declared there: the row stays, with an empty value, so the gap is visible.

2.6 Which rows exist
For each indicator, the required rows are:

(the qualifier combinations declared in CL_INDICATOR.qualifiers) × (the cuts in TAB_PLAN that cover its theme and unit) × (the categories of those cuts) − (anything listed in excluded_breakdowns)

Nothing extra, nothing missing. A cell with no observations is a row with OBS_STATUS=O, not an absent row. This is what makes a file checkable: the validator can compute the set of rows that should exist and compare it with the rows that do.

3.3 Worked example: adding sector of employment

Decide whose characteristic it is. “Sector of an individual’s main job” (EMP_SECTOR, describes IND) and “sector of the household head’s main job” (HHH_SECTOR, describes HHH) are two different variables. The first can break down only individual-level indicators; the second can break down household indicators such as the poverty rate.
Register it in CL_BRK_VAR: describes = IND, applies_to_units = IND, universe = employed persons aged 15–64, classification = ISIC Rev.4, partition = Y, slot_order = 60.

Produce the rows. When the cut is crossed with individual sex, the rows for women also carry SEX=F. When it is crossed with quintile, QUINT has the lower slot_order, so it takes slot 1 and EMP_SECTOR takes slot 2.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
5.1 Code rules

Uppercase ASCII letters, digits and _; start with a letter; at most 32 characters, the Stata variable-name limit. P-codes are used as issued and already comply.
_T and _Z are reserved sentinels and never appear as codes.
A code never changes meaning, and is never reused or deleted. A changed definition means a new code, with the old one DEPRECATED and replaced_by filled. Rewording a label is free.
Breakdown and qualifier categories are <var_code>_<category>. The whole code must still fit in 32 characters, so keep var_code short.
Indicator codes are <THEME>_<SUBJECT>[_<DETAIL>] and contain no poverty line, PPP round, welfare concept, COICOP division, unit or breakdown, because all of those are dimensions. Use POV_HC, never POV_HC_PL420.
In Stata, name the variable holding an indicator after its code in lower case, so no lookup table is needed.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
6.1 Estimation rules

Code the indicator variable as missing for units outside its universe, so they leave both the numerator and the denominator.
Estimate with the survey design declared (weights, strata, PSUs), and use subpopulation estimation for groups rather than dropping observations, so that standard errors stay correct.
Use the weight named in the dictionary (POP = household weight × household size, for person-level statistics computed on household data).
Publish every estimate. Do not blank, round away or drop a small cell; report its N_OBS.
Write values unrounded, in base units.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
6.2 A note on legacy conversions
Files that the converter produces from the current Excel inherit values already rounded to two decimals, and they carry no sample sizes. Such a file sets precision = ROUNDED_2DP in its manifest. The validator then relaxes its aggregation tolerances and does not demand STD_ERR, CI_* or N_OBS. This exemption applies only to converted legacy files, never to new production.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
6.3 How the dashboard shows reliability
Since nothing is suppressed, the dashboard carries the burden of honesty:

Every value is shown with its N_OBS, available on hover, in a details panel or in the downloaded table.
Charts show the confidence interval where one exists.
A cell resting on few records is visually de-emphasized rather than hidden, and OBS_STATUS=O renders as “no observations”, never as zero.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
7.1 Add an indicator

Search CL_INDICATOR for the same concept. If it exists, reuse it. Before creating a code, check whether the difference is a qualifier: a different poverty line, PPP round, welfare concept or COICOP division is never a new indicator. Neither is a population share; that is POP_SH with a breakdown.
If a near-duplicate exists, fill related and related_note on both rows.
Standardize the variables it needs in the harmonized microdata, so that the indicator is a plain aggregate of them (Section 1.4). Record them in source_questionnaire and source_vars, and the program that computes the indicator in program.
Fill every R column and the C columns that apply, including qualifiers and checks.
Produce it for every applicable cut.
Open a pull request (Section 10).

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
7.2 Add a breakdown variable
Follow Section 3.3: decide describes and applies_to_units, write the universe, reuse an international classification if one exists, set slot_order, register the categories, and add the cuts. Expect small N_OBS in fine groups, and publish them anyway with their sample sizes.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
7.3 Add a qualifier variable

Confirm it is a qualifier: the population behind each category is the same one (Section 1.1).
Register it with a slot_order and, if it depends on another qualifier, requires.
Register its categories, with value, basis and valid_with where they apply.
List it in the qualifiers field of every indicator that takes it, naming the allowed categories.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
7.4 Add a country
Follow the order in Section 1.4: metadata first, data last.

CL_AREA: add the country, with its ISO2 code (the P-code prefix) and its currency.
CL_GEO_SCHEME: register every spatial scheme the country will publish, with the local name of each level.
CL_GEO: register the units of each scheme, using the P-codes of the boundary file you will map with.
Indicators: check each indicator in CL_INDICATOR against the country’s survey, and reuse the code wherever the definition holds. Where it does not, register a new code linked to the old one through related and related_note (Section 7.1). Never stretch an existing definition to fit.
Breakdowns and qualifiers: map the survey’s own variable values to the shared codes, in the producer’s program. A country-specific category becomes a child of a shared code (a secondary-city stratum is parent = U), never an unrelated new code.
SURVEYS: add each survey round, with its design, welfare aggregate and national poverty line.
Boundaries: add the ADM0 and ADM1 boundary file and its GEO_SOURCES row (Section 8.4).
TAB_PLAN: add rows only where the country’s cuts differ from the shared ALL rows, for example for its own zone scheme.
Data: produce the data file and manifest for each reference year (Section 6), run the validator, and open one pull request with the metadata and the data together (Section 10).

Every other code comes from the shared codelists.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
section: 8.1 Maps exist for countries and ADM1 only
text:
8.1 Maps exist for countries and ADM1 only
has_geometry = Y is set for ADM0 and ADM1. Every other scheme, including ADM2, zones and agro-ecological zones, is published as tables with no map, no geometry file and no missing-geometry error. Neither Senegal’s zones nor Guinea-Bissau’s agro-ecological zones therefore need polygons.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
8.2 Storage
Boundaries are stored as GeoPackage (.gpkg) files, one per country per boundary vintage, with one layer per level:
geo/boundaries/SEN_CODAB_v02.gpkg     layers: adm0, adm1
Why not shapefiles: a shapefile is 5–6 files that must travel together. Its DBF field names are cut at 10 characters (the current files show cod_versio and adm1_ref_n), its text fields stop at 254 characters, its encoding is declared in a side-car .cpg, and its .prj carries no authority code (the current files say GCS_WGS_1984 with no EPSG number). A GeoPackage is one SQLite file with UTF-8 text, long field names, several layers and an SRS with its authority code, and geopandas, QGIS, ArcGIS and R all read it.
Rules:

Required layer fields: geo_code (matching CL_GEO.code), ref_area, scheme. A name column may be kept for convenience, but CL_GEO is authoritative, and disagreement is a warning, not an error.
CRS: EPSG:4326 in storage. Reproject only for display or area computation.
Hygiene: valid geometries, one feature per code, units covering the country exactly once.
Vintages are explicit. valid_from and valid_to in CL_GEO describe the boundary release a code belongs to, not the period the data cover. SEN’s COD-AB v02 dates from 2024 while the data are for 2021, and that is not an error.
Derived layers are generated, never hand-edited. Simplified display copies live in geo/derived/ and may be rebuilt at any time; the simplification tolerance is kept in the build script.
Size: keep files in git while they are small. Beyond a few MB, use Git LFS or an external store, with the URL and checksum in the registry.

GEO_SOURCES.csv columns: source_id, ref_area, provider, version, valid_on, url, download_date, licence, attribution (the credit line the map must show), crs, file, layers, sha256, status, version_added, notes.

title: AFW 360 data standard and producer guidelines
text:
8.3 Figures
Figures live at assets/figures/<ISO3>/<figure_id>.<ext> and are registered in FIGURES.csv, with columns figure_id, ref_area, time_period, theme, title_en, caption_en, alt_text_en (required: what a screen reader announces), indicators, source, producer, program, licence, file, sha256, status, version_added, notes.
Prefer generating figures from the data; an image is a last resort. Use SVG or PDF for charts, and PNG at twice display size for anything raster. The dashboard asks for a figure_id, not a file name.

12.2 Open decisions

Age cutoff for household heads. The current Youth_HH / Older_HH boundary is undocumented; confirm it before publishing any HHH_AGE_* code.
Quintile definition. National or within-area ranking, person- or household-weighted. The answer goes in CL_BRK_VAR.definition_en.
Governance. Who owns metadata/ and reviews pull requests.
GNB survey metadata. About_GNB.txt contains only a placeholder, so the survey round and its TIME_PERIOD are unknown.

Where variable-level metadata lives. Section 1.4 asks for documentation of every harmonized microdata variable behind an indicator. 4. Value conventions

Levels are stored in the same columns as shares, with no unit or type field. A single number format cannot fit every row.
Values are rounded to 2 decimals at source. Anything below 0.005 is stored as 0.00 and cannot be told apart from a true zero.
An empty cell can mean either “not computed” (wood_dist) or “too few observations in this group” (scattered blanks in small regions). The file does not distinguish the two. Empty must not be read as zero.
Labels contain non-ASCII characters: en-dash – (15–64, Safe drinking water – dry season) and ≥. SDG is written both as SDG 7.1.1 and SDG7.1.1. Matching by typed text is fragile.

6. Discrepancies and data-quality issues

6.1 SEN Departement sheet

It contains the same 14 regions as ADM 1, spelled identically. There is no département-level data in the file.
It is an older or different version of the regional table:

Poverty is at 2017 PPP (Poor at $3.00/day (2017 PPP), Poor at $4.20/day (2017 PPP)) instead of 2021 PPP.
How far its values drift from ADM 1 varies by indicator. Six of the 60 shared indicators are identical (Employed (activ12m, 15–64), Employed in agriculture, Wage-employed, Non-wage employed, HH has internet access, Has health insurance/coverage (couvmal)). Most others differ modestly. The household-enterprise money variables differ heavily: up to 94% for HE revenue per worker, 68% for HE capital stock, 74% for HE costs, and 14.7x for HE profits.

Its indicator set does not match: 82 rows, 60 shared with the other sheets, 22 unique and 37 missing.

Unique rows include raw variable names: (max) con_1 … (max) con_15, (max) ext_emp, npoor300, npoor420.

7. Consistency checks that hold
Checked across every cell of both countries, and correct:

Poor at $3.00/day never exceeds Poor at $4.20/day.
Poverty falls monotonically from Q1 to Q5.
Regional values bracket the national value.
COICOP 1–13 sum to 0.96–1.02, which is what rounding 13 two-decimal shares produces.
Agriculture + industry + services, and food + non-food, sum to about 1; wage + non-wage sums to exactly 1.00.
HH has 0/1/2/3/4+ HE sums to about 1, except on SEN Departement.
HE has any credit access is at least as large as its formal and informal components, except on SEN Departement.

Two notes for anyone re-running these checks:

Scanning for identical columns or rows produces false positives. Some indicator pairs match only because both are near zero everywhere (for example GNB Owns wall AC/split and ≥1 HH member has health coverage). Require the values to vary before calling a pair a duplicate.
The duplicates in 6.2 pass that test: they track each other across the full range.

8. What harmonization will need

A long table with one row per country × breakdown × group × indicator, holding the value.
An indicator dictionary: stable code, label, theme, unit / value type, display format, poverty line, PPP year, source variable.
A geography lookup: admin code, level and display name for every region and zone, replacing name-based matching.

title: Appendix B.2. AFW 360 transition: the contract
text:
The contract is what lets many agents build files and code at the same time without seeing each other’s output. It fixes every code, path, header, interface and expected count that they must agree on in advance.
This document is the readable reference. The contract itself is the set of machine-readable files in contract/. Each package card repeats the rules its package needs, so agents do not read this document unless a card says so.

title: Appendix B.2. AFW 360 transition: the contract
text:
2.1 Rules for codes

A code matches ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,31}$.
_T (total) and _Z (not applicable) are reserved sentinels. They never appear in a codelist, and no code starts with them. GEO and URBANISATION are never _Z.
A category code is <var_code>_<category>. Its variable is looked up through the var_code column, never by parsing the prefix (gap t).
TBD is a reserved token for a required value that cannot be known from the inputs. It is allowed only in a column that has no codelist, and only on a DRAFT row. The validator warns on it there, and gives an error once the row is no longer DRAFT (gap d).
Everything the transition creates is status = DRAFT, with version_added = 0.1.0.

2.4 Geography

ADM0 codes (SN, GW) are geometry-only. They are registered in CL_GEO but never used in the GEO column of a data row, where the whole country is _T (gap k).
SN01 and SN13 are invalid as delivered. They are repaired with sf::st_make_valid() under sf_use_s2(FALSE), from the plain (non-_em) shapefiles (gap u).
Three zone names come from headers truncated at 32 characters. Their full names are TBD inside name_en until a producer confirms them (gap v).

text:
3.3 Field grammars

CL_INDICATOR.qualifiers is _Z when the indicator takes no qualifier. Otherwise it holds VAR:CODE,CODE entries, separated by one space, in qualifier slot_order. VAR:* allows every category.
CL_INDICATOR.checks holds tokens separated by one space, from the vocabulary in Section 4.4.
LEGACY_LABELS.assert_rule is EQUALS:<series_id> or ONE_MINUS:<series_id>, optionally followed by tol=<number>. The default tolerance is 0. duplicate_of holds the same target series_id. In the triage seed these point at row IDs such as L008; WP09 translates them.
LEGACY_LABELS.sheet is a sheet name, or * for National, ADM 1 and ZAE.
In LEGACY_OVERRIDES, sheet, column and legacy_label accept * for “every”. WITHHOLD wins over COMMENT.
Registry paths are relative: GEO_SOURCES.file to geo/boundaries/, FIGURES.file to assets/figures/, and TEXT.file to content/text/.

title: Appendix B.2. AFW 360 transition: the contract
text:
4.4 Checks vocabulary and tolerances (gap h)
The tokens are RANGE_0_1, RANGE_NONNEG, AGG_SUM, AGG_BRACKET, AGG_NPOP_MEAN, SUM_TO_1_OVER:<QUAL_VAR>, SUM_TO_1_OVER_BRK, EQUALS_NPOP_RATIO, MONOTONE_IN:POVLINE and NONE.

The parent of a row is the row of the same series in the cut TOTAL. Provenance (series_id, cut_id) comes from required_rows().
For ROUNDED_2DP files, h = 0.005 × scale:

a sum of k children against its parent tolerates (k + 1) × h;
a closure over k categories tolerates k × h (for COICOP, ±0.065);
a bracket tolerates h on each side;
monotonicity gets no tolerance.

Every comparison is abs(deviation) <= tolerance + 1e-9.
AGG_BRACKET (the parent lies within [min child − h, max child + h]) stands in for AGG_NPOP_MEAN while N_POP is absent. The two N_POP rules are skipped with an INFO finding on legacy files.
A group with a withheld or empty child is skipped with a WARN. A closure over a partial category set is skipped with an INFO.

These rules were run against the raw workbooks with these tolerances, and the legacy data break none of them.
